counterevidence_considered.description: All 24 ponds were filled from the same source water at a single field station in a single season, which is the closest candidate for dependence among units. This is a shared-origin consideration, not a repeated entry of any pond into the procedure, and the description explicitly states the ponds stood apart and never exchanged water, so it does not instantiate the issue class under review.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: shared source water; ponds physically isolated and never exchanged water

evidence.description: Inspection of data/input.csv shows 24 data rows with 24 distinct pond_id labels P01 through P24 and zero duplicates, so no independent unit enters the dataset more than once.

The workflow enforces pond_id uniqueness with a hard error before analysis, and builds the 2x2 contingency table by counting each row exactly once, so each pond contributes exactly one entry to the Fisher exact test.
evidence.observed_value: duplicate pond_id raises ValueError; Counter tallies one (canopy, outcome) pair per row

evidence.description: The reported counts and p-value are exactly reproducible from one-row-per-pond data: hand tally gives shaded 9 persisted / 3 collapsed and open 3 persisted / 9 collapsed, and the two-sided Fisher exact p-value from hypergeometric probabilities with 12/12 margins is 2 x (0.017898 + 0.001611 + 0.0000532 + 0.00000037) = 0.039126, matching the report to six decimals. No inflation from repeated unit entry is present in the reported result.
evidence.observed_value: table [[9,3],[3,9]], odds ratio 9.000, p = 0.039126 (verified by hand)

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Two-sided Fisher exact test on 24 independent mesocosm ponds: shaded ponds persisted in 9 of 12 cases versus 3 of 12 open ponds (sample odds ratio 9.000, p = 0.039126), so canopy shading is associated with higher persistence at the 5% level.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by searching for any route through which a pond could enter the Fisher exact test more than once: I checked every pond_id in data/input.csv for duplicates (P01 through P24, all distinct), checked the workflow for row expansion, merging, resampling, or per-covariate replication before the test (there is none; the Counter tallies each row exactly once and read_ponds raises on duplicate pond_id), and recomputed the contingency table and two-sided Fisher p-value by hand from the CSV, obtaining [[9,3],[3,9]] and p = 0.039126, which matches the report exactly and confirms every count corresponds to a distinct pond. I also considered whether covariates (volume, stocking density, temperature) constituted repeated measurements within a pond; the description states they describe the pond as a whole and they are unused in the test. No mechanism of repeated authorized independent-unit entry could be demonstrated.
